patch.value: Evaluate proposer transfer on a statistically powered tracker corpus

The bounded recursive-improver acceptance uses two independent meta trackers, below the unchanged ten-sample outer gate minimum. Plan a larger independent public tracker/task benchmark with an explicit power analysis, preserve chronological and meta/audit separation, and repeat equal-budget proposer comparisons without relaxing the promotion gate.

The bounded recursive-improver acceptance uses two distinct meta trackers, below the unchanged ten-sample outer gate minimum; item-level inner bounds are also underpowered on the small chronological cohorts. Plan a larger public tracker/task benchmark with an explicit power analysis, account for correlated fleet work, preserve chronological and meta/audit separation, and repeat equal-budget proposer comparisons without relaxing the promotion gate.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Plan: freeze public commit-pinned tracker-disjoint development/meta/audit sources; declare a 0.10 transfer effect, 0.01 promotion margin, alpha 0.05 and target power 0.80 before measuring. Use bounded paired tracker means with task and generation Bonferroni correction. Preserve existing promotion gates and refuse underpowered evidence. Seal replayable corpus/split/evaluation context in SDK-owned items and native history; run one CPU-niced bounded real generation, report all refusals honestly.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Corpus frozen before scoring: 31 public MIT source pins, 19 development tasks, 16 meta tasks and 11 audit tasks; corpus digest 7156cf8c85b9941e12e42632c08f27419af69b7b3ee8824545c35def3fee9d49. One unverifiable directory excluded; private/hosted sources never opened. Conservative declared power requires 3062 held-out trackers per task; the available fleet cannot meet this. Proceeding with one bounded diagnostic generation, not claiming powered no-transfer evidence.
